concerns: The proposed national preference is too strong for a neutral everyday cue: “bulan depan” is also ordinary in Malaysian Malay, while “bulan hadapan” is understood in Indonesia.
response.cue_rationale: Both answers naturally mean the calendar month immediately after the current one.
material_concerns: The pair may mislead learners into treating “bulan depan” as Indonesian-only and “bulan hadapan” as Malaysian-only.

preference_risk.rationale: “Bulan depan” is an ordinary same-sense alternative in Malaysian Malay as well as Indonesian, weakening the claimed national preference.

response.rationale: Both forms express the same calendar-month sense, but the contrast is weak because “bulan depan” is common in Malaysia too; “bulan hadapan” is a useful Malaysian formal preference rather than an exclusive national equivalent.
response.shared_synonym_rationale: “Bulan depan” is plausibly ordinary in both varieties, especially in Malaysian colloquial usage, so it can defeat the proposed preference contrast.
